relations.myth: Prohibition and judgment of Molech worship
relations.note: YHWH prohibits offerings to Molech and threatens offenders with expulsion.

relations.myth: Repudiation of the Jerusalem Molech rite
relations.note: YHWH condemns passing children to Molech and denies commanding it.

relations.myth: Children passed to Molech at Baal's high places
relations.note: Molech rites occur at Baal's high places without narrated divine interaction.
Solomon builds adjacent high places for Chemosh and textually uncertain Molech.
Ashtoreth and Molech appear in the same catalogue of foreign cults.
Milcom and Molech occur in the same foreign-cult narrative.
Molech is traditionally equated with Milcom, possibly through textual corruption.

relations.myth: Tent of Moloch and star of Rephan
relations.note: Moloch and Rephan appear together in the Greek Amos tradition.
Later harmonization equates Moloch with the Punic recipient Baʿal Hammon.
Later harmonization identifies Moloch with El, Kronos, and Saturn.
relations.source: Philo of Byblos and later harmonization

relations.note: Modern scholarship disputes whether Malik-like deities are cognates of biblical Molech.
A disputed reconstruction links Molech indirectly through ancient Malik–Nergal equations.

relations.myth: War in Heaven and infernal council
relations.note: Milton's fallen Moloch rebels against God and advocates renewed open war.
